guide_enrichment.narrative: We are not treating Maryland’s fast start as proof that its early production will carry over unchanged. Malik Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards against UConn, while Na’eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. combined for 236 receiving yards. That performance is meaningful context, but our longer-run efficiency numbers remain skeptical of Maryland’s passing offense against a more capable Nebraska pass defense.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Nebraska’s rushing offense against Maryland’s front. Maryland allowed only 38.5 rushing yards per game and recorded 10 sacks through its first two games, but Nebraska’s rushing efficiency presents a substantially different test. The question is whether Maryland’s early defensive production reflects a sustainable strength or an opponent-dependent start. Our numbers favor Nebraska in that area, which limits the case for taking Maryland, while the overall price remains too close to our expectation to create enough value. We pass.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, producing 475 total yards, 27 first downs and no turnovers.
Against UConn, Maryland passed for 350 yards and rushed for 125 yards and three touchdowns.
Maryland's defense held UConn to 223 total yards, including 67 rushing yards, and recorded five sacks.
Maryland had second-quarter scoring drives of 92 and 91 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: In the 2025 game against Nebraska, quarterback Malik Washington completed 27 of 37 passes for 249 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions; he also rushed seven times for nine yards.
Running back DeJuan Williams had 10 carries for 36 yards and a touchdown plus five receptions for 36 yards against Nebraska in 2025.
Cornerback Jamare Glasker recorded an interception and two tackles for loss against Nebraska in 2025.
Linebacker Zahir Mathis recorded a sack for a 10-yard loss against Nebraska in 2025.

quarterback.fact: Sophomore Malik Washington is Maryland's returning starting quarterback and started each of the first two games of 2026 after starting all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns at UConn, including a Maryland-record 18 consecutive completions.
Through two games in 2026, Washington was 53-of-72 for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.
Transfer backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed four of five passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards in the opener against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's offensive line against UConn consisted of left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright; the unit blocked for 475 total yards.
Amory Hills made his first Maryland start at left guard against UConn after transfer Tellek Lockette started the opener at that position.
Left tackle Rahtrel Perry entered the guide with 39 career starts, including 14 at Maryland, while center Michael Hershey and right tackle Isaiah Wright each had 14 Maryland starts.
Transfer receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. combined for 18 receptions, 236 yards and two touchdowns at UConn.
Gladding had eight catches for 130 yards and a touchdown at UConn and had 14 catches for 187 yards and two touchdowns through two games.
Durr recorded 10 catches for 106 yards and a touchdown at UConn and had 16 catches for 147 yards through two games.
Running backs Harry Dalton III and Iverson Howard each scored in Maryland's first two games; Dalton had two rushing touchdowns at UConn, while Howard had 55 rushing yards and one touchdown.

Maryland added 17 offseason transfers, including receivers Gladding, Durr and Ejani Shakir; running backs Dalton and Terrez Worthy; tight end Preston Howard; offensive lineman Tellek Lockette; and quarterbacks Cardell Williams and Jack Capaldi.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's UConn defensive starters included Lavon Johnson, Eyan Thomas, Nahsir Taylor and Sidney Stewart in the front; Trey Reddick and Daniel Wingate at linebacker; and Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson, Jordan Scruggs, Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs in the secondary grouping.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble at UConn after leading Maryland with seven sacks as a freshman in 2025.
DD Holmes led Maryland with 2.5 sacks through two games, while Eyan Thomas and transfer Derrick LeBlanc each had two sacks.
Freshman Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble at UConn, with DD Holmes recovering the fumble.

Maryland added defensive-line transfers Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon Parker and Jayvon Parker from Washington, along with defensive back Amari Jackson from Boston College.

coaching_changes.fact: Clint Trickett became Maryland's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach during the 2026 offseason after serving as Jacksonville State's offensive coordinator in 2025.
Matt Barnes returned to Maryland as special teams coordinator after two seasons as Mississippi State's co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Maryland added Randy Starks as defensive line coach and Kyle Schmitt as tight ends coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Maryland averaged 560.5 total yards, 315.5 passing yards, 245 rushing yards and 50 points per game.
Maryland converted 55.2 percent of its third downs through two games and had not committed a turnover.
Maryland scored nine rushing touchdowns through its first two games, including six against Hampton and three against UConn.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Maryland allowed 154 total yards, 38.5 rushing yards, 115.5 passing yards and seven points per game.
Maryland recorded 10 sacks through its first two games, the most in the Big Ten at that point.
Maryland held its first two opponents to a 26.9 percent third-down conversion rate and no red-zone scores.
Maryland had held 18 consecutive opponents below 300 passing yards, its longest such streak since a 19-game run from 2005 through 2007.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Sean O'Haire made field goals of 26 and 36 yards against Hampton and 19 yards against UConn.
Maryland averaged 19.33 yards per punt return through two games.

other_relevant.fact: Maryland's 2026 schedule lists the Nebraska game for Oct. 3 in Lincoln as the Terrapins' second Big Ten game, following the Sept. 26 conference opener against UCLA.
